skill.name: biopython
skill.description: Guide for using Biopython to analyze molecular biology data. It covers sequence files, alignments, NCBI services, BLAST, structures, phylogenetics, and advanced analysis.
skill.summary: Build practical molecular biology workflows with Biopython modules and focused examples.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, biological identifiers, and placeholder credentials. Fixed-path writes can overwrite files, package installation changes the environment, and online BLAST can disclose sequences to NCBI. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Fixed output filenames can overwrite existing analysis files.
remediation.suggestion: Ask users to choose output paths and check for existing files before opening any destination in write mode.

remediation.issue: Online BLAST sends sequence data to an external NCBI service.
remediation.suggestion: Request explicit consent before submission and recommend local BLAST for proprietary, clinical, or otherwise sensitive sequences.

remediation.issue: API key examples assign credentials directly in source code.
remediation.suggestion: Show environment-based credential loading and warn users not to commit API keys into scripts or notebooks.

remediation.issue: The setup example installs a package into the active Python environment.
remediation.suggestion: Request confirmation before installation and recommend a dedicated virtual environment with a pinned Biopython version.

content.value_statement: Bioinformatics tasks require many specialized formats, modules, and service rules. This skill provides focused Biopython guidance for reliable sequence, structure, database, and phylogenetic workflows.
actual_capabilities: Create, transform, translate, and inspect DNA, RNA, and protein sequences with Bio.Seq.
Read, write, and convert FASTA, GenBank, FASTQ, alignment, PDB, and mmCIF files.
Search and fetch NCBI records through Bio.Entrez with rate-limit guidance.
Run online or local BLAST workflows and parse, filter, and summarize BLAST results.
Parse protein structures and calculate structural measurements with Bio.PDB.
Build, modify, compare, and display phylogenetic trees with Bio.Phylo.
limitations: Biopython and required scientific dependencies must be installed separately.
NCBI and online BLAST workflows require network access, identification, and compliance with service limits.
The skill provides guidance and examples, but it does not validate biological conclusions.
External tools such as local BLAST, DSSP, or alignment programs may require separate installation.

use_cases.title: Convert Sequencing Files
use_cases.description: Convert laboratory sequence files between supported formats while preserving identifiers, annotations, and quality data.

use_cases.title: Automate NCBI Research
use_cases.description: Search publications and biological records, then fetch selected entries with responsible rate handling.

use_cases.title: Teach Reproducible Analysis
use_cases.description: Create clear exercises for sequence analysis, alignment, structural biology, and phylogenetic methods.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Biopython to analyze this {DNA_OR_PROTEIN_SEQUENCE}. Report length, composition, and relevant transformations. Explain each result in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Sequence File
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Biopython workflow that converts {INPUT_FILE} from {INPUT_FORMAT} to {OUTPUT_FORMAT}. Preserve available annotations and report rejected records.

prompt_templates.title: Retrieve NCBI Records
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Bio.Entrez workflow for {SEARCH_QUERY} in {NCBI_DATABASE}. Include email setup, batching, rate limits, error handling, and reproducible output.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Comparative Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Biopython pipeline for {SEQUENCE_SET}. Include validation, alignment, BLAST filtering, phylogenetic analysis, caching, failure recovery, and documented parameters.

output_examples.input: Summarize the DNA sequence ATGCGCGTAA and identify its basic properties.
output: The sequence starts with ATG and ends with TAA.

output_examples.input: Plan a GenBank-to-FASTA conversion for sample.gb without losing record identifiers.
output_examples.output: The plan validates GenBank records, preserves each primary identifier, writes FASTA output, and reports records with missing sequences.

output_examples.input: Describe a responsible PubMed search workflow for CRISPR delivery studies.
output_examples.output: The workflow sets the required Entrez email, searches PubMed in batches, caches identifiers, fetches selected records, and handles network failures.

best_practices: Validate the declared file format and inspect a small sample before processing a complete dataset.
Set an Entrez email, respect NCBI limits, cache responses, and retry transient failures carefully.
Record software versions, input sources, parameters, and genetic code choices for reproducible analysis.
anti_patterns: Do not load large sequence collections into memory when an iterator can process records incrementally.
Do not submit sensitive sequences to online services without explicit approval from the data owner.
Do not hardcode API keys, personal identifiers, or machine-specific paths in shared scripts.

faq.question: Does this skill install Biopython?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation guidance, but Biopython and optional external tools must be installed in your environment.

faq.question: Which sequence formats are supported?
faq.answer: Biopython supports many formats, including FASTA, GenBank, FASTQ, EMBL, Clustal, PHYLIP, PDB, and mmCIF.

faq.question: Can it access NCBI databases?
faq.answer: Yes. Bio.Entrez can search and fetch NCBI records when network access and the required email identification are available.

faq.question: Can it run BLAST locally and online?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance covers NCBI web searches, local BLAST commands, and parsing common BLAST result formats.

faq.question: Is online BLAST suitable for confidential sequences?
faq.answer: Not without approval. Use a local BLAST database when sequences are proprietary, clinical, or subject to data-handling restrictions.

faq.question: Does the skill verify scientific conclusions?
faq.answer: No. Users must review data quality, parameters, assumptions, and biological interpretation for their specific study.
